subject: sociology
title: Sampling, Ethics and Real Studies
welcome_lead: Pick your sample, follow the BSA Code, and put methods to work in classic studies.
meta_desc: GCSE Sociology adventure on sampling techniques, the BSA ethics code and applied research examples.
final_note: Always link a method to a real study and a real ethical worry.

concepts.def: A smaller group chosen to represent the target population.
Everyone has an equal chance of being picked.
Sample mirrors key proportions, e.g. gender.
Each respondent suggests the next, useful for hidden groups.
Participants agree after knowing the research.

walkthroughs.body_html: You can't ask everyone. Random samples are unbiased but may miss small groups. Stratified samples match the population's make-up. Snowball sampling is vital for studying hidden groups like drug users.

The British Sociological Association demands informed consent, the right to withdraw, anonymity, no harm and honesty. Covert observation can breach these — though it may be the only way to study a closed group.

Willis (1977) used participant observation with 12 working-class 'lads' to show how they resisted school. Carlen (1988) used unstructured interviews with 39 female offenders. Match method to question.
